text:
anya: quick dump — I sketched a compact-queue handoff + starvation mitigation approach. want quick sanity check before i turn it into an RFC. main idea: avoid big compaction spikes by moving *ownership* of a small inflight set between queue owners using lightweight transfer tokens instead of full global rebalancing.

matt: curious — how do tokens avoid thrashing? if ownership flips frequently we might amplify latency tail. is there a cooldown or lease?

anya: yes — tokens carry a lease TTL and a soft-grace period. owner that receives token can accept or reject. if rejected we fall back to current eviction path. goal is to make common-case fast (handshake) and rare-case conservative (reject -> controlled compaction).

jin: tradeoffs: faster handoff reduces peak compaction but increases coordination ops (RPCs). we need to measure overhead at 10k qps and with microbursts. also need a heartbeat to extend lease for in-progress long requests.

anya: agreed. my thinking: token RPC is O(1) per lane change, piggybacked on existing admission messages where possible. heartbeat only for requests above threshold (e.g., >200ms). small requests never heartbeat.

sophie: observability notes — add counters: `handoff.attempts`, `handoff.accepted`, `handoff.rejected`, `handoff.latency_ms` and histograms for `compaction.duration_ms` pre/post rollout. also annotate traces with `handoff.token_id` for debug.

tom: for latency SLOs we should gate on request size: tiny fastpath (<=32 tokens) gets immediate dedicated slot; tokens only for medium ones. avoids touching the fastpath. less risk of regressing 99p.

anya: good call. we'll keep the microburst fastpath unchanged. tokens only apply to lanes that are subject to compaction-induced stalls.

matt: what about K/V cache eviction signal? earlier experiments showed compaction racing with KV reads. do tokens include a kv-affinity hint so handoff owner can prefetch or avoid evicting those keys?

jin: maybe include `kv_hint` bitset (coarse) in token — small footprint but useful for prewarming. downside: more state to transmit and interpret. test both with/without hint to measure win.

anya: rough pseudo-proto:```
message TransferToken {
  string id = 1;
  uint32 lease_ms = 2;
  repeated uint64 kv_hint_hashes = 3; // optional coarse hints
  uint32 request_count = 4;
}
```
handshake: sender -> receiver: `offer(token)`; receiver: `accept(token_id)` or `reject(token_id, reason)`; on accept sender releases queued refs gradually (N ms drip) to avoid spike.

sophie: rollout plan suggestion — canary 1% of tenants, monitor `handoff.rejected` and 99p latency for those tenants, then 10% w/ increased telemetry retention. also extra alert if `compaction.duration_ms` increases.

matt: agreed. also add a debug flag to force-reject to simulate worst-case and validate fallback code paths.

runtime-bot: perf-run #712: compact-queue-unit-tests passed; integration perf harness queued.

anya: next steps: I'll write a short RFC + proto sketch incorporating small-request fastpath exemption, token lease/backoff heuristics, and observability. thanks for feedback — will tag y'all on draft. :raised_hands:
